subject: Urban Planning
title: Japanese Zoning: A Global Alternative
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Japanese Zoning: A Global Alternative.

hook.text: Japan has 12 national zones. Each allows everything the zone below it allows, plus more. It's cumulative, not exclusive.

buildup.text: A residential zone in Japan allows homes, offices, small shops, and restaurants. Mixed use is the default.

discovery.text: Only the most industrial zone bans residential. Everywhere else, someone can live. Housing is never excluded.

twist.text: Japanese neighborhoods look chaotic to Americans — a house next to a convenience store next to a temple. It works.

climax.text: Tokyo is one of the most affordable major cities in the developed world. Flexible zoning keeps supply high.

punchline.text: Allow everything. Ban almost nothing. Housing stays affordable.

quiz.question: What makes Japanese zoning fundamentally different from American zoning?
options: Japan doesn't have any zoning laws at all
Japanese zones are cumulative — each allows everything below it plus more
Japan requires all buildings to be the same height in each zone
